A multi-angle rearview camera also makes parking and maneuvering easier, while the Civic's excellent visibility and manageable dimensions make it particularly easy to live with in both city and suburban environments.

The Touring combines the desirable turbocharged engine with leather seating, upgraded technology, premium audio, navigation, and additional comfort features, making it an excellent choice for someone who wants Civic efficiency and dependability without giving up luxury.

COMING SOON!
2019 Chevrolet Trax LT 94,835 Miles
This 2019 Chevrolet Trax LT is a practical, affordable compact SUV that packs a surprising amount of versatility into an easy-to-drive package. Finished in sharp Mosaic Black Metallic with 94,835 miles, this Trax is nicely equipped with the LT Convenience Package, giving you upgraded comfort and convenience features that make it a great choice for commuting, a first vehicle, or everyday family transportation.
Power comes from Chevrolet's 1.4L turbocharged 4-cylinder engine paired with a 6-speed automatic transmission and front-wheel drive. The turbocharged engine provides responsive performance while keeping efficiency in mind, and its compact dimensions make the Trax especially easy to maneuver through traffic and fit into tight parking spaces.
The Mosaic Black Metallic exterior has a clean, sporty appearance complemented by aluminum wheels, roof-mounted luggage rails, privacy glass, heated power mirrors, automatic headlights, daytime running lights, and LED-accented taillamps. Its hatchback-style design gives you the versatility of an SUV without the bulk of a larger crossover.
Inside, the LT Convenience Package adds several worthwhile upgrades, including a power driver's seat with lumbar adjustment, premium synthetic/cloth seating, leather-wrapped steering wheel, and keyless start. You'll also find remote start, cruise control, air conditioning, power windows and locks, keyless entry, steering-wheel audio controls, a cargo shade, and a fold-flat front passenger seat for carrying longer items.
Technology includes Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, Bluetooth, satellite radio, Wi-Fi hotspot capability, Chevrolet Connected Access, a 6-speaker audio system, and a backup camera. Smartphone integration makes it easy to bring your compatible navigation, music, messages, and other apps along for the drive.
The Trax is also equipped with traction and stability control, anti-lock brakes, a comprehensive airbag system, tire-pressure monitoring, child safety locks, and a security system. Combined with the elevated seating position and backup camera, it's a comfortable and approachable SUV for everyday driving.
With 94,835 miles, this 2019 Chevrolet Trax LT offers a lot of useful equipment in an affordable, manageable package. The turbocharged engine, LT Convenience Package, power driver's seat, remote start, smartphone integration, backup camera, roof rails, and flexible cargo area make it a solid choice for anyone looking for SUV practicality without stepping up to a larger and more expensive vehicle.

2016 Mercedes-AMG GLE63 | Rare Hyacinth Red | 61K Miles | $103K MSRP

2016 Mercedes-AMG GLE63 with 61,000 miles, finished in rare Hyacinth Red over Black Leather. I've owned the car for the past 3 years and have taken good care of it throughout my ownership. I'm selling it privately.

This is the 550-hp GLE63 with AMG's hand-built M157 5.5L biturbo V8, AMG Performance 4MATIC and 7-speed AMG transmission. It's incredibly fast and sounds amazing. These 5.5L biturbo AMG models represent a very different era of Mercedes-AMG from today's smaller-displacement/hybrid performance vehicles. The engine and exhaust are stock with no mods.

Original MSRP was $103,840. It's well equipped with the Night Package, 21-inch matte-black AMG wheels, panoramic roof, Blind Spot Assist, Lane Keeping Assist, surround-view cameras, heated steering wheel, Anthracite Poplar wood trim, black running boards, black emblems and factory trailer hitch. The car has Pirelli Scorpion tires with approximately 70% tread remaining.

I've put more than $10,000 into service and maintenance during my ownership, in addition to regular oil changes. Some of the more significant work includes:

9/21/23 Oil pump control valve $3,083
7/1/24 Brake rotors & pads $1,226
4/11/25 Spark plugs $1,738
11/13/25 Brake pads $314
3/26/26 Leak detection pump $330
9/8/25 Starter replacement & A/C recharge $3,657

The car has been professionally detailed and is ready for its next owner. There are some minor cosmetic imperfections you would expect on a 10-year-old vehicle, but overall it's a clean well-cared-for GLE63.

Serious inquiries welcome.

description:
**2009 Subaru Forester 5-Speed AWD 111,*** Miles The Good Kind of Weird**

If you know Subarus, you know what this is: an old-school, 5-speed, AWD Forester that absolutely **does not care what the weather is doing.** Snow? Ice? Mud? Gravel? She just goes.

111,*** miles, 5-speed manual, AWD, roof rack, and Rally Armor mud flaps. Mechanically, this thing has been a tank and has been incredibly dependable for me. It has been one of those cars I could just hop in and drive without thinking twice.

Cosmetically, she's a 2009 Subaru that has lived an actual life. A few dents here and there, plus a handful of very small rust spots, but **nothing major and no nasty rust issues.** The sunroof has had a crack since I bought it. I've always said I'd fix it if it ever leaked...and it still hasn't leaked, so apparently we're conducting a long-term engineering experiment.

The stereo has developed the classic Subaru/electrical gremlin where it randomly shorts out. Sometimes it works, sometimes it apparently has other plans.

One tire currently has Fix-a-Flat in it and should be properly repaired or replaced. It holds air, and honestly I don't even notice anything until around 70 mph.

Other than those quirks, this thing has been an absolute beast and a ton of fun to own. It's the kind of old Subaru that makes you understand why people get weirdly attached to these cars.

**Why am I selling it?**
Because I need to make room for something that can tow a trailer. Otherwise, I'd probably keep driving this thing until the wheels literally fall off.

If you're looking for a pristine 2009 Forester, this isn't it. If you're looking for a **well-loved, honest, 5-speed AWD Subaru that still has plenty of life left and is ridiculously good in the snow**, this might be your kind of car.

Come drive it. You'll probably understand.
